title: Document and gate the dangling provenance left by the 2026-09-10 repo recreation
description: Every @opum-ai/lore* version published before 0.6.1 carries SLSA provenance pinning a commit the 2026-09-10 repo delete/recreate destroyed. 0.6.0's attestation resolves to gitCommit 59ba30e497f8e98aa6c6be022d9363fd718fb4ee at refs/tags/v0.6.0; GitHub answers 422 'No commit found for SHA' for it, and its build run 34393976910 is 404. On npmjs.com this surfaces as a provenance link that cannot find the commit, which reads as tampering to anyone who does not know the history was rebuilt. The SHA still resolves in local clones' loose objects, so a git cat-file check wrongly says it is fine. Nothing repairs the existing links short of republishing. quest-cli confirmed the identical shape across all 8 of its pre-0.6.1 versions and already shipped the documented-not-repaired response in QCLI-267: a GitHub Release plus a --pre/--post provenance gate in release.yml. lore-cli has no equivalent. Filed 2026-09-13 out of the 0.6.1 release investigation; deliberately kept OUT of that release.

acceptanceCriteria.text: release-publishing.md carries a section explaining that pre-0.6.1 provenance links are permanently dangling, names the 2026-09-10 recreation as the cause, and states plainly that this is expected rather than tampering
The doc warns that the destroyed SHAs still resolve in local clones loose objects, so git cat-file is not a valid check -- the live GitHub API is
release.yml carries a provenance gate comparable to quest-cli QCLI-267s --pre/--post check, so a future history rewrite is caught at release time rather than discovered on npmjs.com
A GitHub Release exists for the affected tags, or the decision not to create one is recorded with its reasoning

comments.body:
SOURCE TEXT TO ADAPT, and one way it does NOT transfer.

quest-cli shipped the equivalent section on 2026-09-13: quest-cli PR #42, file
docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md, section "## A 404 on an old gitHead is
expected, not tampering" (commit be0c21e; not on their dev yet at this writing, so read it
from that commit, not from a checkout). They explicitly offered it for adaptation and said
nothing in it is quest-cli-specific except package and repo names.

THAT LAST PART IS NOT QUITE TRUE FOR US, and it is the reason this note exists. Their
section is framed end to end around npm's `gitHead` field. lore-cli's published versions do
not have one -- checked every version of @opum-ai/lore-darwin-arm64 on the registry, and
`gitHead` is absent from all of them, including 0.3.0, 0.5.0 and 0.6.0. Adapting their
prose by swapping names would produce a section telling readers to check a field that does
not exist on our packages, and a reader who checked and found nothing would reasonably
conclude the warning was stale.

lore-cli's dangling reference lives on a DIFFERENT surface: the SLSA provenance
attestation, not the packument. Retrieve it as

  curl -s "https://registry.npmjs.org/-/npm/v1/attestations/@opum-ai%2flore-darwin-arm64@0.6.0"

then base64-decode the sigstore bundle's dsseEnvelope.payload and read
predicate.buildDefinition.resolvedDependencies[0].digest.gitCommit, alongside
externalParameters.workflow.ref. For 0.6.0 that is gitCommit
59ba30e497f8e98aa6c6be022d9363fd718fb4ee at refs/tags/v0.6.0, and
`gh api repos/opum-ai/lore-cli/commits/59ba30e4...` answers 422. The build run named in
predicate.runDetails.metadata.invocationId (34393976910) is 404 for the same reason.

WHAT DOES TRANSFER VERBATIM: their "check this from the live GitHub API, never from a local
clone" paragraph, including the git cat-file trap. That reasoning is identical for us and is
the single most valuable line in the section -- keep it.

ALSO WORTH COPYING: their framing that this is a documentation entry and not a task because
the cure is worse than the condition (npm forbids republishing a version; re-pointing a tag
would still disagree with the immutable published metadata; the tarballs, checksums and
signatures are all intact and correctly signed -- only the commit the provenance names has
stopped existing). AC#4 on this task should almost certainly resolve as "decision not to
create a GitHub Release, recorded with reasoning" on the same grounds.

FOR AC#3, their forward gate is scripts/release-provenance.mjs wired into release.yml as
--pre/--post (QCLI-267). lore-cli has no equivalent. Build ours against the attestation
surface described above rather than gitHead, or it will check a field we never publish.

AC#4 RESOLVED AS A RECORDED DECISION, NOT A GITHUB RELEASE, 2026-09-13.

The criterion allowed either. Choosing the second, on the same grounds quest-cli reached independently in QCLI-267 and opum-agent in OPAG-125 -- three arrivals at the same answer:

  1. npm forbids republishing a version, so the published metadata cannot be corrected at the source.
  2. Re-pointing a tag would still disagree with that immutable published metadata, and a tag moved after the fact to match a broken provenance link reads as a cover-up rather than a fix.
  3. The artifacts are all INTACT: tarballs, checksums and signatures are correct and correctly signed. Only the commit the provenance NAMES has stopped existing. The cure is worse than the condition.

A GitHub Release for v0.6.1 does exist (cut 2026-09-13T22:53Z), but that is not what this criterion is about -- the affected tags are the PRE-0.6.1 ones, v0.6.0 and earlier, and no Release is being cut for those.

VERIFIED FIRST-PARTY while reviewing the doc half, because the section is only worth having if its commands work:
  - The documented retrieval recipe runs and yields gitCommit 59ba30e497f8e98aa6c6be022d9363fd718fb4ee at refs/tags/v0.6.0.
  - gh api repos/opum-ai/lore-cli/commits/59ba30e4... answers HTTP 422 "No commit found for SHA".
  - git cat-file -p on the SAME sha in this checkout prints a healthy commit object -- tree, parent, author. The false pass the section warns about, reproduced.

ONE CORRECTION TO MY OWN BRIEF, found by the agent doing the work: the attestations endpoint returns TWO attestations, npm publish/v0.1 AND slsa.dev/provenance/v1. My recipe omitted selecting between them, which yields nulls on decode. The shipped doc selects on predicateType. Worth knowing for anyone writing the gate against the same surface.

finalSummary:
All four criteria met. The gate took two rounds and the second one is why it is worth having.

WHAT SHIPPED. A --pre/--post provenance gate (scripts/release-provenance.mjs) wired into release.yml, plus the runbook section (#26). It distinguishes three outcomes deliberately: attestation ABSENT passes with a loud recorded note (0.6.1 and 0.6.2 genuinely ship unattested because OIDC is dead -- LCLI-482, open); attestation PRESENT and resolvable passes; attestation PRESENT pinning a commit the LIVE GitHub API cannot resolve fails. A gate that failed on the absent case would have blocked the only publish path that currently works and been deleted on first contact.

THE FIRST ROUND WAS NOT GOOD ENOUGH, and adversarial review caught two defects that would each have made the gate worthless in the opposite direction:

  1. A FALSE WARRANT. --pre checked only the launcher package per historical release, justified in the header as 'verify-versions asserts one version across every manifest, so the launcher is a sound probe'. verify-versions asserts version/license/author/os/cpu/pin equality and says NOTHING about commits. Worse, release.yml's own publish_or_skip exists precisely so a release can complete across two dispatches from two different commits -- so six packages could pin commit X and the launcher pin Y, with the gate only ever seeing Y. The gate was confidently wrong about the exact scenario it exists for. Now sweeps every package of every scanned release, memoised per repo@sha so the normal case still costs one API call. The old warrant is preserved in the header AS A THING THAT WAS FALSE, so it cannot come back.

  2. A TRUE POSITIVE BRICKED EVERY FUTURE RELEASE. --pre re-checks published history, so one post-baseline dangle would exit 1 forever with publish unreachable -- and the error text told the operator not to do the one thing the design permits. Absolute message, conditional design, no sanctioned exit, so the operator deletes the gate. Now there is an acknowledge_dangling_provenance dispatch input taking a REFERENCE, not a boolean: a waiver names what it is accountable to, is listed and warned about, does not persist, and a hardcoded waiver in the workflow is a TEST FAILURE.

ALSO FIXED: detection no longer rests on an English substring GitHub controls -- a 422 is corroborated by fetching the repository itself (422 + repo resolves 200 = the commit is gone), with the wording used only to label the log line, and a live canary against the real destroyed SHA runs on every bun test. Zero versions checked is now 'This is NOT a pass' rather than the literal string 'Passed.'. Per-package propagation windows, and no wait at all when no package carries an attestation -- which with LCLI-482 open is every release, so the common path costs zero seconds instead of seven times three minutes. timeout-minutes on both jobs and a 20s AbortSignal on every request. A script defect exits 3 named as ours rather than being swallowed as a remote outage. The baseline literal is pinned by a test. provenance-post now runs when publish FAILED, which is the mixed-commit case.

VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, not on the agent's report: rebased and ran the gate tests (45 pass, 0 fail); applied continue-on-error: true to provenance-pre myself and confirmed the wiring test FAILS -- the old tests passed straight through that, which is the single most likely way a noisy gate gets defanged; ran --pre live against the real registry and watched it sweep all 7 packages of 0.6.1 (not the launcher sample), report absent, and exit 0.

ONE DISAGREEMENT ACCEPTED FROM THE IMPLEMENTER: I had listed an 'if:' that never matches as a pass-through vector. It is not -- GitHub skips the dependents of a skipped job, so publish would be skipped too. It fails closed. The assertion is kept anyway because it is cheap, but the rationale was corrected rather than recorded wrong.

AC#3 resolves as a RECORDED DECISION rather than a GitHub Release for the pre-0.6.1 tags, on grounds quest-cli (QCLI-267) and opum-agent (OPAG-125) reached independently: npm forbids republishing, a re-pointed tag would still disagree with immutable published metadata and reads as a cover-up, and the artifacts are intact -- only the commit the provenance NAMES stopped existing.

NOT IN SCOPE, filed separately as LCLI-486: scripts/ is excluded from both lint and typecheck, so this 835-line file has no static analysis at all. That gap belongs to the repository, not to this gate.
